content: Selenic acid is a chemical compound with the molecular formula H₂SeO₄. It can also be represented as (HO)₂SeO₂, which highlights that the selenium atom is bonded to four oxygen atoms. According to Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion (VSEPR) theory, the selenium atom in selenic acid adopts a tetrahedral geometry. Selenic acid is synthesized by oxidizing selenium dioxide (SeO₂) with hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂). To obtain the anhydrous form of selenic acid as a crystalline solid, the resulting solution is evaporated under vacuum at temperatures below 140°C. Selenic acid, like sulfuric acid, is a strong acid. It is highly hygroscopic and extremely soluble in water. Concentrated solutions of selenic acid are viscous in nature. Crystalline forms of monoand di-hydrates of selenic acid are also known. However, unlike sulfuric acid, selenic acid (H₂SeO₄) is a sufficiently strong oxidizing agent to release chlorine gas from chloride ions, during which it is reduced to selenious acid (H₂SeO₃). Selenic acid reacts with barium salts to form a precipitate of barium selenate (BaSeO₄), which is analogous to barium sulfate (BaSO₄). However, calcium selenate is more soluble in water compared to calcium sulfate. Additionally, hot selenic acid has the ability to dissolve gold.
